deck.name: English Core · C1
deck.summary: Precise, academic and professional vocabulary. Advanced.

senses.definition: large in amount, size or importance

translations.zh: 大量的；相当大的；重要的

examples.text: The library received a substantial donation of books.

translations.zh: 图书馆收到了一大批捐赠的图书。

senses.definition: including everything that is relevant

examples.text: The report offers a comprehensive review of the field.

translations.zh: 这份报告对该领域做了全面综述。

senses.usageNote: Do not confuse with 'comprehensible', which means able to be understood.

senses.definition: money that a business or government receives

examples.text: Ticket sales are the museum's main source of revenue.

translations.zh: 门票销售是博物馆的主要收入来源。

senses.definition: the act of supplying something that people need

examples.text: The town has good provision for young children.

translations.zh: 这个镇为幼儿提供了良好的设施和服务。

senses.usageNote: The plural 'provisions' can mean supplies of food for a journey.

senses.definition: a law or set of laws made by a government

examples.text: New legislation requires all bikes to have lights at night.

translations.zh: 新法规要求所有自行车夜间必须有车灯。

senses.usageNote: Uncountable: say 'a piece of legislation' or 'new legislation', not 'a legislation'.

senses.definition: the process of changing from one state to another

examples.text: The transition from primary to secondary school can be hard.

translations.zh: 从小学升入中学的过渡可能会很困难。

senses.definition: an idea or belief about something

examples.text: She rejected the notion that girls are bad at maths.

translations.zh: 她反对女孩数学不好的观念。

senses.definition: happening after something else

examples.text: The first test was hard, but subsequent tests were easier.

translations.zh: 第一次考试很难，但之后的考试容易些。

senses.usageNote: 'Subsequent to' is a formal way of saying 'after'.

senses.definition: something that stays or continues after a person or period has gone

examples.text: The scientist left a lasting legacy of important discoveries.

translations.zh: 这位科学家留下了一系列重要发现的持久遗产。

senses.definition: to produce a result, crop or profit

examples.text: The experiment yielded some surprising results.

translations.zh: 这个实验得出了一些令人惊讶的结果。

senses.definition: the amount of something that is produced

examples.text: This year's apple yield was the best ever.

translations.zh: 今年的苹果产量是有史以来最好的。

senses.definition: to say or believe that something is caused by something else

examples.text: He attributes his good health to daily exercise.

translations.zh: 他把自己的健康归功于每天锻炼。

senses.usageNote: Pattern: 'attribute A to B'. As a noun, 'an attribute' /ˈætrɪbjuːt/ means a quality: Patience is a useful attribute.

senses.definition: very new and different, or affecting the most basic parts of something

examples.text: The school made radical changes to its timetable.

translations.zh: 学校对课程表进行了彻底的改革。

senses.definition: to form or be something; to be the parts that make up something

examples.text: Girls constitute more than half of the class.

translations.zh: 女生占了班级一半以上。

senses.definition: a story or a description of a series of events

examples.text: The book's narrative jumps between the past and the present.

translations.zh: 这本书的叙事在过去与现在之间来回跳跃。

senses.definition: advanced and complicated; or having experience and good taste

translations.zh: 复杂精密的；老练的；高雅的

examples.text: The robot uses sophisticated sensors to avoid obstacles.

translations.zh: 这个机器人利用精密的传感器避开障碍物。

senses.definition: to expect something and often prepare for it

examples.text: We anticipate a large number of visitors at the fair.

translations.zh: 我们预计集市会有大量游客。

senses.usageNote: Follow with a noun or '-ing', not 'to': 'anticipate meeting them', not 'anticipate to meet them'.

senses.definition: a possible effect or result of an action; something suggested indirectly

examples.text: Think about the implications of your decision.

translations.zh: 想想你的决定可能带来的影响。

senses.usageNote: Often plural: 'the implications of something'.

senses.definition: allowed by law or rules, or fair and reasonable

examples.text: Being ill is a legitimate reason for missing school.

translations.zh: 生病是缺课的正当理由。

senses.definition: important and well known, or easy to see

examples.text: The poster was placed in a prominent position near the door.

translations.zh: 海报被贴在门口显眼的位置。

senses.definition: easily hurt or harmed, physically or emotionally

examples.text: Newborn animals are very vulnerable in the cold.

translations.zh: 刚出生的小动物在寒冷中非常脆弱。

senses.usageNote: Common pattern: 'vulnerable to something'.

senses.definition: the act of getting something, especially knowledge or skills; something you have bought

examples.text: Reading widely helps with the acquisition of new vocabulary.

translations.zh: 广泛阅读有助于习得新词汇。

senses.usageNote: 'Language acquisition' is the standard term for how people learn a language.

senses.definition: to keep or continue to have something

examples.text: The old building has retained much of its charm.

translations.zh: 这座老建筑保留了许多原有的魅力。

senses.definition: to publicly support an idea or way of doing things

examples.text: Doctors advocate eating more vegetables and less sugar.

translations.zh: 医生提倡多吃蔬菜、少吃糖。

senses.usageNote: As a verb, it takes a direct object: 'advocate a change', not 'advocate for a change' in formal British English. The noun 'an advocate' /ˈædvəkət/ has a different last syllable.

senses.definition: to put a plan or decision into action

examples.text: The school implemented a new recycling scheme.

translations.zh: 学校实施了一项新的回收计划。

senses.usageNote: As a noun, 'an implement' /ˈɪmplɪmənt/ is a tool, e.g. garden implements.

senses.definition: neither very large nor very small; not extreme

examples.text: Doctors recommend moderate exercise several times a week.

translations.zh: 医生建议每周进行几次适度的锻炼。

senses.usageNote: As a verb it is pronounced /ˈmɒdəreɪt/ and means to make something less extreme.

senses.definition: the way you notice or understand something; a belief about what something is like

examples.text: The trip changed my perception of city life.

translations.zh: 这次旅行改变了我对城市生活的看法。

senses.definition: a factor or number that can change

examples.text: Temperature is an important variable in the experiment.

translations.zh: 温度是这个实验中的一个重要变量。

senses.definition: likely to change often

examples.text: The weather in spring is highly variable.

senses.definition: strong and able to keep working under difficult conditions

examples.text: The findings are robust across several datasets.

translations.zh: 这些发现在多个数据集上都很稳健。

senses.definition: an unfair preference for or against someone or something

examples.text: A good referee must judge without bias.

translations.zh: 优秀的裁判必须不带偏见地判罚。

senses.usageNote: Use 'bias against' (unfair dislike) or 'bias towards/in favour of' (unfair liking).

senses.definition: to improve the quality or value of something

examples.text: Good lighting can enhance the look of a room.

translations.zh: 好的灯光能提升房间的效果。

senses.usageNote: 'Enhance' is used for things, not people: 'enhance your skills', not 'enhance you'.

senses.definition: to consist of or be made up of

examples.text: The team comprises five boys and six girls.

translations.zh: 这支队伍由五个男孩和六个女孩组成。

senses.usageNote: Say 'is comprised of' or 'comprises', but not 'comprises of' — a very common mistake.

senses.definition: how likely it is that something will happen

examples.text: Regular exercise reduces the likelihood of heart problems.

translations.zh: 经常锻炼能降低患心脏病的可能性。

senses.usageNote: Common phrase: 'in all likelihood', meaning almost certainly.

senses.definition: felt or done by two or more people towards each other, or shared by them

examples.text: Good teamwork depends on mutual respect.

translations.zh: 良好的团队合作取决于相互尊重。

senses.usageNote: 'A mutual friend' is a friend that two people both know.

senses.definition: a description of a possible situation or series of events

examples.text: In the worst scenario, the match will be cancelled.

translations.zh: 最坏的情况下，比赛会被取消。

senses.usageNote: Common phrase: 'worst-case scenario'. It does not mean a film script in everyday English.

senses.definition: to make something start to happen

examples.text: Dust can trigger a sneezing fit.

senses.definition: real or basic, but not easy to notice

examples.text: We need to find the underlying cause of the problem.

translations.zh: 我们需要找到问题的根本原因。

senses.definition: to state firmly that something is true

examples.text: He asserted that the answer in the book was wrong.

translations.zh: 他坚称书上的答案是错的。

senses.usageNote: 'Assert yourself' means to act confidently so that people notice your opinions.

senses.definition: to express or communicate an idea or feeling

examples.text: Music can convey feelings that words cannot.

translations.zh: 音乐能表达言语无法表达的情感。

senses.definition: important or interesting enough to be noticed

examples.text: The town is notable for its colourful houses.

translations.zh: 这个小镇以色彩缤纷的房屋而著称。

senses.definition: so strong or interesting that it demands attention or agreement

translations.zh: 令人信服的；引人入胜的

examples.text: There's compelling evidence that spacing works.

translations.zh: 有令人信服的证据表明间隔重复有效。

senses.definition: to stop happening or doing something

examples.text: The noise ceased as soon as the teacher walked in.

translations.zh: 老师一走进来，吵闹声就停止了。

senses.usageNote: Formal. In everyday speech use 'stop'. 'Cease to amaze' means something keeps surprising you.

senses.definition: something that encourages you to do something

examples.text: Free stickers are an incentive for children to read more.

translations.zh: 免费贴纸能激励孩子们多读书。

senses.usageNote: Use 'an incentive to do something' or 'an incentive for someone'.

senses.definition: the ideas, styles or activities that most people accept as normal

examples.text: Electric cars are becoming part of the mainstream.

translations.zh: 电动汽车正逐渐成为主流。

senses.definition: the range of things that a subject or activity deals with; also the chance to do something

examples.text: That question is beyond the scope of this lesson.

translations.zh: 那个问题超出了这节课的范围。

senses.usageNote: 'Scope for' means opportunity: 'There is scope for improvement.'

senses.definition: existing as a natural and permanent part of something

examples.text: Difficulty is inherent to the item, not to the day you study it.

translations.zh: 难度是词条固有的属性，与你哪天学习无关。

senses.definition: decided by personal choice or chance rather than by reason or rule

examples.text: The deadline felt arbitrary.

translations.zh: 这个截止日期显得很随意。

senses.definition: to give a share of something for a particular purpose

examples.text: The teacher allocated each group a different topic.

translations.zh: 老师给每组分配了不同的课题。

senses.definition: a usual or accepted way of behaving or doing something

examples.text: Working from home has become the norm for many people.

translations.zh: 居家办公已成为许多人的常态。

senses.definition: a new business or activity that involves some risk

examples.text: Their bakery is a joint venture between two sisters.

translations.zh: 他们的面包店是两姐妹合伙开的。

senses.definition: to go somewhere unfamiliar or possibly unsafe

examples.text: We ventured into the forest to look for mushrooms.

translations.zh: 我们冒险进入森林寻找蘑菇。

senses.definition: general agreement among a group

examples.text: There is no consensus on the optimal review interval.

translations.zh: 关于最佳复习间隔尚无共识。

senses.usageNote: 'Consensus' already means general agreement — 'general consensus' is redundant.

senses.definition: an important discovery or development

examples.text: Scientists made a breakthrough in cleaning plastic from the sea.

translations.zh: 科学家在清除海洋塑料方面取得了突破。

senses.usageNote: Say 'make a breakthrough in something'.

senses.definition: done on purpose, not by accident

examples.text: It was a deliberate choice to start the story at the end.

translations.zh: 从结尾开始讲故事是有意为之的选择。

senses.usageNote: As a verb /dɪˈlɪbəreɪt/, it means to think carefully before deciding.

senses.definition: very small in amount or degree

examples.text: The storm caused only minimal damage to the school.

translations.zh: 暴风雨只对学校造成了极小的损坏。

senses.definition: to keep something going over a period of time

examples.text: It is hard to sustain your concentration for three hours.

translations.zh: 连续三个小时保持专注是很难的。

senses.definition: the amount by which something is less than needed, especially money

examples.text: The club had a deficit of two hundred pounds this year.

translations.zh: 俱乐部今年亏空了两百英镑。

senses.definition: legal responsibility for something, or a person or thing that causes problems

examples.text: The company accepted liability for the damaged goods.

translations.zh: 公司承担了货物受损的责任。

senses.definition: only; being the one and only

examples.text: Reading was his sole purpose for visiting the library.

translations.zh: 他去图书馆的唯一目的就是看书。

senses.definition: the bottom surface of your foot or shoe

examples.text: The soles of my trainers are worn out.

translations.zh: 我运动鞋的鞋底磨破了。

senses.definition: while; during the time that, or although (formal, British)

examples.text: Please wait here whilst I find the manager.

translations.zh: 我去找经理的时候，请在这里等一下。

senses.usageNote: 'Whilst' is mainly British and more formal than 'while'; the meaning is the same.

senses.definition: to have enough space for someone or something; to provide what someone needs

translations.zh: 容纳；为……提供住宿；照顾到（需要）

examples.text: The hall can accommodate about three hundred people.

translations.zh: 这个礼堂能容纳大约三百人。

senses.usageNote: Spelling: double 'c' and double 'm' — a very common spelling mistake.

senses.definition: lasting for a long time or happening again and again

examples.text: She has chronic back pain from sitting badly.

translations.zh: 由于坐姿不良，她患有慢性背痛。

senses.usageNote: 'Chronic' is about how long something lasts, not how serious it is. The opposite is 'acute'.

senses.definition: the force that keeps something moving or developing

examples.text: The campaign to save the library is gaining momentum.

translations.zh: 拯救图书馆的活动势头越来越大。

senses.usageNote: Common collocations: 'gain momentum', 'lose momentum', 'keep up the momentum'.

senses.definition: a large group of things, often shown in an attractive way

examples.text: The shop sells a wide array of colourful kites.

translations.zh: 这家店出售各种各样色彩鲜艳的风筝。

senses.usageNote: Common phrase: 'a wide/vast array of'.

senses.definition: to pay someone for a loss, or to balance a bad effect with a good one

examples.text: His hard work compensated for his lack of experience.

translations.zh: 他的勤奋弥补了经验的不足。

senses.usageNote: Use 'compensate for something' to mean 'make up for'.

senses.definition: an area of knowledge or activity; an internet address name

examples.text: Grammar is her domain — ask her anything.

translations.zh: 语法是她的专长——尽管问她。

senses.definition: to make an action or process easier

examples.text: Clear signs facilitate movement around the museum.

translations.zh: 清晰的标识让人们在博物馆里走动更方便。

senses.usageNote: You facilitate a process, not a person: 'facilitate learning', not 'facilitate students'.

senses.definition: quickly and easily, or willingly

examples.text: The information is readily available online.

translations.zh: 这些信息在网上很容易获得。

senses.definition: an act of breaking a rule, law or agreement

examples.text: Sharing the password was a breach of the club's rules.

translations.zh: 泄露密码违反了俱乐部的规定。

senses.usageNote: Common collocations: a breach of contract, a security breach, a data breach.

senses.definition: connected with what is morally right or wrong

examples.text: Is it ethical to keep wild animals in small cages?

translations.zh: 把野生动物关在小笼子里合乎道德吗？

senses.definition: to include something as part of something larger

examples.text: The design incorporates ideas from all the students.

translations.zh: 这个设计融合了所有学生的想法。

senses.usageNote: Use 'incorporate A into B'.

senses.definition: a set of official rules for how to behave or do something

examples.text: Staff must follow the safety protocol in the lab.

translations.zh: 员工在实验室必须遵守安全规程。

senses.definition: suggested but not stated directly

examples.text: There was an implicit criticism in her question.

translations.zh: 她的问题里含有隐含的批评。

senses.definition: to gradually collect or increase over time

examples.text: Dust had accumulated on the old books in the attic.

translations.zh: 阁楼上的旧书积满了灰尘。

senses.definition: to obey a rule, order or request

examples.text: Visitors must comply with the museum's rules.

translations.zh: 参观者必须遵守博物馆的规定。

senses.usageNote: Always 'comply with something'.

senses.definition: an idea that tries to explain something but has not yet been proved

examples.text: Our hypothesis is that plants grow faster in blue light.

translations.zh: 我们的假设是植物在蓝光下长得更快。

senses.usageNote: The plural is 'hypotheses' /haɪˈpɒθəsiːz/.

senses.definition: to make something stronger, or to support an idea or feeling

examples.text: Regular practice reinforces what you learn in class.

translations.zh: 经常练习能巩固课堂所学的内容。

senses.definition: a group of things made or dealt with at the same time

examples.text: We baked a batch of twenty cookies.

translations.zh: 我们烤了一炉共二十块饼干。

senses.definition: able to exist or work together without problems

examples.text: This charger is not compatible with my tablet.

translations.zh: 这个充电器和我的平板电脑不兼容。

senses.usageNote: Use 'compatible with something'.

senses.definition: to use something or someone for a particular purpose

examples.text: The team deployed new software to track the orders.

translations.zh: 团队启用了新软件来跟踪订单。

senses.definition: a person who starts their own business

examples.text: The young entrepreneur started a company selling eco-friendly bags.

translations.zh: 这位年轻的创业者开了一家销售环保袋的公司。

senses.definition: the quality of being honest and having strong moral principles

examples.text: She is a person of great integrity.

translations.zh: 她是一个非常正直的人。

senses.definition: the great size or importance of something

examples.text: Nobody realised the magnitude of the task at first.

translations.zh: 起初没有人意识到这项任务有多艰巨。

senses.definition: very great or strong; showing deep understanding

examples.text: The internet has had a profound effect on education.

translations.zh: 互联网对教育产生了深远的影响。

senses.definition: one of the parts that something is divided into

examples.text: She divided the orange into segments.

translations.zh: 她把橙子掰成了一瓣一瓣的。

senses.definition: to happen or make something happen faster

examples.text: The new software accelerated our progress on the project.

translations.zh: 新软件加快了我们项目的进度。

senses.definition: having enough skill to do something well

examples.text: She is a competent swimmer and can swim a kilometre.

translations.zh: 她游泳很不错，能游一公里。

senses.usageNote: 'Competent' usually means 'good enough', not 'excellent'.

senses.definition: what happens or is used automatically if you do not choose something else

examples.text: The default language on the app is English.

translations.zh: 这个应用的默认语言是英语。

senses.usageNote: 'By default' means automatically, or because nothing else happened: We won by default.

senses.definition: to use something fully for your benefit; to treat people unfairly for profit

examples.text: The team exploited their opponents' weak defence.

translations.zh: 这支球队充分利用了对手防守的薄弱环节。

senses.usageNote: It can be positive (exploit an opportunity) or negative (exploit workers), so check the context.

senses.definition: to cause someone or something to be in a certain state

examples.text: The heavy snow rendered the roads impossible to use.

senses.usageNote: A formal pattern: 'render + object + adjective', e.g. 'render something useless'.

senses.definition: having more than one possible meaning, so it is unclear which is intended

translations.zh: 模棱两可的；含义不明的

examples.text: The wording of the clause is ambiguous.

translations.zh: 该条款的措辞含义不明。

senses.usageNote: 'Ambiguous' means open to two readings; 'ambivalent' means having mixed feelings. They are not synonyms.

senses.definition: an official check of accounts or of how something is done

examples.text: The company has a financial audit every year.

translations.zh: 这家公司每年都要进行财务审计。

senses.definition: a strong feeling of care for people who are suffering

examples.text: She showed great compassion towards the injured animal.

translations.zh: 她对这只受伤的动物表现出极大的同情。

senses.usageNote: Use 'compassion for/towards someone'.

senses.definition: to make something start

examples.text: Our class initiated a project to plant more trees.

translations.zh: 我们班发起了一个多种树的项目。

senses.definition: a good quality that deserves praise or reward

examples.text: Each idea should be judged on its merits.

translations.zh: 每个想法都应根据其本身的价值来评判。

senses.definition: to deserve something

examples.text: The suggestion merits further discussion.

translations.zh: 这个建议值得进一步讨论。

senses.definition: the effort to achieve something; also an activity you enjoy

examples.text: Hiking and cycling are popular outdoor pursuits.

translations.zh: 徒步和骑行是很受欢迎的户外活动。

senses.usageNote: Common phrase: 'in pursuit of', e.g. 'in pursuit of happiness'.

senses.definition: never having happened before

examples.text: Demand reached unprecedented levels.

translations.zh: 需求达到了史无前例的水平。

senses.definition: connected with beauty and how things look

examples.text: The new bridge is useful, but it also has great aesthetic appeal.

translations.zh: 新桥很实用，也很有美感。

senses.definition: very strange and unusual

examples.text: I had a bizarre dream about talking fish.

translations.zh: 我做了一个关于会说话的鱼的怪梦。

senses.usageNote: Don't confuse with 'bazaar' (a market), which sounds the same.

senses.definition: the act of obeying a rule or request

examples.text: All toys must be in compliance with safety standards.

translations.zh: 所有玩具都必须符合安全标准。

senses.definition: to admit that something is true, often unwillingly

examples.text: He conceded that his sister had won fairly.

senses.definition: to become or make something smaller or less important

examples.text: The pain diminished after a few hours.

translations.zh: 几个小时后疼痛减轻了。

senses.definition: clear and exact, leaving no doubt about the meaning

examples.text: The instructions were explicit: no phones in the exam.

translations.zh: 说明写得很明确：考试时不准带手机。

senses.usageNote: The opposite is 'implicit' (suggested but not said directly).

senses.definition: using new ideas or methods

examples.text: The team designed an innovative water filter.

translations.zh: 团队设计了一款创新的净水器。

senses.definition: a limit or rule that controls how something can be done

examples.text: We must work within the parameters of our budget.

translations.zh: 我们必须在预算范围内开展工作。

senses.definition: not obvious, and so hard to notice or describe

translations.zh: 微妙的；细微的；不易察觉的

examples.text: There is a subtle difference between the two colours.

translations.zh: 这两种颜色之间有细微的差别。

senses.usageNote: The 'b' is silent: /ˈsʌtl/.

senses.definition: to make something necessary or appropriate

examples.text: A small scratch doesn't warrant a trip to the hospital.

translations.zh: 一点小擦伤不需要去医院。

senses.definition: negative or harmful

examples.text: Heavy rain had an adverse effect on the harvest.

translations.zh: 大雨对收成造成了不利影响。

senses.usageNote: Don't confuse 'adverse' (harmful: adverse effects) with 'averse' (unwilling: I'm not averse to hard work).

senses.definition: to work together with someone to produce something

examples.text: Two classes collaborated on a big wall painting.

translations.zh: 两个班合作完成了一幅大型壁画。

senses.usageNote: Use 'collaborate with someone on something'.

senses.definition: a standard used to judge or decide something

examples.text: Originality is one criterion for judging the stories.

translations.zh: 原创性是评判这些故事的标准之一。

senses.usageNote: The plural is 'criteria'. 'A criteria' is a common mistake.

senses.definition: to show or describe someone or something in a picture or story

examples.text: The painting depicts a busy market in winter.

translations.zh: 这幅画描绘了冬日里热闹的集市。

senses.definition: having many carefully arranged parts or details

translations.zh: 精心制作的；复杂的；详尽的

examples.text: They built an elaborate sandcastle with towers and bridges.

translations.zh: 他们搭了一座有塔楼和桥的精致沙堡。

senses.usageNote: As a verb /ɪˈlæbəreɪt/, 'elaborate on something' means to give more details.

senses.definition: serious, worrying or unpleasant

translations.zh: 严峻的；令人不快的；阴沉的

examples.text: The weather forecast for the weekend looks grim.

translations.zh: 周末的天气预报看起来很糟糕。

senses.definition: a set of methods used for studying or doing something

examples.text: The report describes the methodology used in the survey.

translations.zh: 这份报告描述了调查所用的方法。

senses.definition: to control something with rules, or to control the speed or amount of something

examples.text: Sweating helps the body regulate its temperature.

translations.zh: 出汗帮助身体调节体温。

senses.definition: official permission, or an official punishment for breaking a rule

examples.text: The trip went ahead with the sanction of the head teacher.

translations.zh: 在校长的批准下，这次旅行如期进行。

senses.usageNote: Confusingly, it can mean both approval and punishment; the context tells you which.

senses.definition: a method used to achieve something

examples.text: The coach changed tactics in the second half.

translations.zh: 教练在下半场改变了战术。

senses.usageNote: Usually plural: 'tactics'. A 'tactic' is a short-term method; a 'strategy' is a long-term plan.

senses.definition: to make something or someone gradually weaker or less effective

examples.text: Constant criticism can undermine a child's confidence.

translations.zh: 不断的批评会削弱孩子的自信心。

senses.definition: able to work successfully

examples.text: Is that a viable alternative?

translations.zh: 那是个可行的替代方案吗？

senses.definition: the freedom to make your own decisions

examples.text: The teacher gave each group autonomy to choose their project.

translations.zh: 老师让各小组自主选择课题。

senses.definition: to form an idea or plan in your mind

examples.text: The idea for the story was conceived during a long train ride.

translations.zh: 这个故事的构思是在一次长途火车旅行中产生的。

senses.usageNote: Common adjective: 'inconceivable' (impossible to imagine).

senses.definition: to say that something is true; to compete

examples.text: The scientist contends that the results need more testing.

translations.zh: 这位科学家认为这些结果需要更多测试。

senses.usageNote: 'Contend with' means to deal with a difficulty: We had to contend with heavy rain.

senses.definition: to stop something from continuing normally

examples.text: Snow disrupted train services across the country.

translations.zh: 大雪扰乱了全国的火车运行。

senses.definition: a system in which people or things are organised by level of importance

examples.text: There is a clear hierarchy in the school's leadership.

translations.zh: 学校的领导层有明确的层级结构。

senses.definition: official permission or an order to do something

examples.text: The committee has a mandate to improve school meals.

translations.zh: 委员会获授权改善学校伙食。

senses.definition: something added to improve or complete something else

examples.text: The website is a useful supplement to the textbook.

translations.zh: 这个网站是教科书的有益补充。

senses.usageNote: As a verb it is pronounced /ˈsʌplɪment/: 'supplement your diet with fruit'.

senses.definition: to check that something is true or correct

examples.text: Please verify your email address before logging in.

translations.zh: 登录前请验证你的电子邮件地址。

senses.definition: logically connected and easy to follow

examples.text: She gave a coherent account of what happened.

translations.zh: 她条理清楚地讲述了发生的事。

senses.definition: a strong hope to achieve something

examples.text: Her aspiration is to become a marine scientist.

translations.zh: 她的志向是成为一名海洋科学家。

senses.definition: a product that is bought and sold, or something useful and valuable

examples.text: Time is a precious commodity for busy parents.

translations.zh: 对于忙碌的父母来说，时间是宝贵的东西。

senses.definition: meant to be kept secret

examples.text: Your exam results are confidential.

translations.zh: 你的考试成绩是保密的。

senses.definition: to give part of your work or responsibility to someone else

examples.text: A good leader knows how to delegate tasks.

translations.zh: 好的领导懂得如何委派任务。

senses.usageNote: As a noun /ˈdelɪɡət/, 'a delegate' is a person sent to represent a group.

senses.definition: to help something develop; to look after a child who is not yours for a period

examples.text: Team sports foster a sense of cooperation.

translations.zh: 团队运动能培养合作意识。

senses.definition: to become involved in a situation to stop or change it

examples.text: The teacher intervened to stop the argument.

senses.definition: a way of dealing with a problem, or a treatment for a minor illness

examples.text: Honey and lemon is a popular remedy for a sore throat.

translations.zh: 蜂蜜柠檬水是治疗喉咙痛的常用方法。

senses.definition: to correct or improve something bad

examples.text: The council promised to remedy the problem quickly.

translations.zh: 议会承诺会尽快解决这个问题。

senses.definition: done according to a careful plan and in a fixed order

examples.text: We need a systematic approach to learning vocabulary.

translations.zh: 我们需要一种系统的方法来学习词汇。

senses.definition: possible to do without great difficulty

examples.text: Thirty reviews a day is feasible; three hundred is not.

translations.zh: 一天三十次复习是可行的，三百次则不然。

senses.definition: to make small changes to improve a text or rule

examples.text: We amended the report after the teacher's comments.

translations.zh: 根据老师的意见，我们修改了报告。

senses.usageNote: Don't confuse 'amend' (change) with 'make amends' (do something to show you are sorry).

senses.definition: the main or largest part of something; a large size

examples.text: The bulk of the work was done by volunteers.

translations.zh: 大部分工作是由志愿者完成的。

senses.usageNote: 'Buy in bulk' means to buy large amounts at once, usually more cheaply.

senses.definition: to go well with something and make it better

examples.text: The red scarf complements her grey coat nicely.

translations.zh: 红围巾和她的灰外套搭配得很好。

senses.usageNote: Don't confuse 'complement' (go well together) with 'compliment' (say something nice).

senses.definition: to say the opposite of what someone else has said; to disagree with facts

examples.text: The new results contradict the earlier findings.

translations.zh: 新结果与早先的发现相矛盾。

senses.definition: a situation where you must make a difficult choice

examples.text: I was in a dilemma about which club to join.

translations.zh: 我在加入哪个俱乐部的问题上左右为难。

senses.usageNote: A dilemma is a hard choice between two options, not just any problem.

senses.definition: something that exists as a separate unit

examples.text: The two schools are now one entity.

translations.zh: 这两所学校现在合为一体了。

senses.definition: a sudden large increase, or a sudden strong movement forward

examples.text: There was a surge in bike sales during the summer.

senses.definition: the level at which something starts to happen; also the entrance to a room

examples.text: Children have a low pain threshold when they are tired.

translations.zh: 孩子们疲倦时对疼痛的忍耐度较低。

senses.usageNote: 'On the threshold of' means about to start something new.

senses.definition: to officially end a law, system or custom

examples.text: The school abolished its old rule about wearing hats indoors.

translations.zh: 学校废除了在室内戴帽子的旧规定。

senses.definition: to succeed in reaching a goal or level, usually after effort

examples.text: She attained the highest grade in the class.

translations.zh: 她获得了全班最高的成绩。

senses.usageNote: More formal than 'reach' or 'get'. Common with: attain a goal, a level, a standard.

senses.definition: to happen at the same time as something else

examples.text: My birthday coincides with the first day of spring.

translations.zh: 我的生日恰好是春天的第一天。

senses.usageNote: Use 'coincide with something'. The noun is 'coincidence'.

senses.definition: to think carefully about something for a long time

examples.text: She sat by the lake, contemplating her future.

translations.zh: 她坐在湖边，思考着自己的未来。

senses.usageNote: Follow with '-ing', not 'to': 'contemplate moving', not 'contemplate to move'.

senses.definition: able to make decisions quickly; very important for the result

examples.text: A good captain needs to be decisive.

senses.definition: allowed to do or receive something because you meet the conditions

examples.text: Children under twelve are eligible for free entry.

translations.zh: 十二岁以下的儿童可以免费入场。

senses.usageNote: Use 'eligible for something' or 'eligible to do something'.

senses.definition: connected with public money or a business's money

examples.text: The company's fiscal year ends in March.

translations.zh: 公司的财政年度在三月结束。

senses.definition: connected with courts of law and judges

examples.text: The judicial system should treat everyone fairly.

translations.zh: 司法制度应当公平对待每一个人。

senses.usageNote: Do not confuse with 'judicious', which means showing good judgement.

senses.definition: very small and not important

examples.text: The new rules made only a marginal difference.

translations.zh: 新规则只带来了微小的变化。

senses.definition: an area of activity, interest or knowledge

examples.text: Travelling to Mars is no longer in the realm of fantasy.

translations.zh: 去火星旅行已不再只是幻想。

senses.usageNote: The 'ea' is pronounced /e/, as in 'head'.

senses.definition: belonging separately to each of the people or things mentioned

examples.text: After lunch, the pupils returned to their respective classrooms.

translations.zh: 午饭后，学生们回到了各自的教室。

senses.usageNote: Do not confuse with 'respectful', which means showing respect.

senses.definition: all the people who work for a company or in a country

examples.text: Half of the company's workforce works from home.

translations.zh: 公司一半的员工在家办公。

senses.definition: based on observation or experiment rather than on theory alone

examples.text: FSRS was fitted to empirical review data.

translations.zh: FSRS 是基于实证复习数据拟合出来的。

senses.definition: completely silly or unreasonable

examples.text: It seemed absurd to wear a coat on such a hot day.

translations.zh: 在这么热的天穿外套似乎很荒唐。

senses.definition: a system with many complicated rules and processes that slow things down

examples.text: There is too much bureaucracy involved in getting a new library card.

translations.zh: 办一张新借书证的手续太繁琐了。

senses.definition: to collect information from different places and put it together

examples.text: We compiled a list of our favourite books.

translations.zh: 我们整理了一份最喜欢的书单。

senses.definition: to keep someone or something within limits

examples.text: Please confine your answer to one page.

translations.zh: 请将答案限制在一页之内。

senses.usageNote: Often passive: 'be confined to bed' means you must stay in bed because you are ill.

senses.definition: a person or thing with the same role in a different place or group

examples.text: Our head teacher met her counterpart from a school in Spain.

translations.zh: 我们的校长会见了西班牙一所学校的校长。

senses.definition: to invent a plan, system or method

examples.text: The students devised a clever way to save water.

translations.zh: 学生们想出了一个巧妙的节水方法。

senses.usageNote: Don't confuse the verb 'devise' /z/ with the noun 'device' /s/.

senses.definition: serious discussion or writing about a subject

examples.text: The book adds to public discourse about climate change.

translations.zh: 这本书丰富了关于气候变化的公众讨论。

senses.definition: an earlier case or action used as an example or rule for later ones

examples.text: The ruling set an important precedent.

translations.zh: 该裁决确立了一个重要先例。

senses.usageNote: Stressed on the first syllable, unlike 'president', which it is often confused with in writing.

senses.definition: the quality of being clear and easy to understand

examples.text: Your essay needs more clarity in the conclusion.

translations.zh: 你文章的结论部分需要更清晰。

senses.definition: to grow crops; to develop a skill or quality

examples.text: Reading every day cultivates good concentration.

translations.zh: 每天阅读能培养良好的专注力。

senses.definition: to experience something difficult for a long time; to continue to exist

examples.text: The explorers endured freezing temperatures for weeks.

translations.zh: 探险家们忍受了数周的严寒。

senses.definition: to grow or develop well and successfully

examples.text: The plants flourished in the warm, sunny garden.

translations.zh: 植物在温暖而阳光充足的花园里长得很茂盛。

senses.definition: a situation that is strange or funny because it is the opposite of what you expect

translations.zh: 讽刺；反语；具有讽刺意味的事

examples.text: The irony is that the fire station caught fire.

translations.zh: 具有讽刺意味的是，消防站着火了。

senses.definition: required by a rule, so you must do it

examples.text: Wearing a helmet is mandatory on the climbing wall.

translations.zh: 在攀岩墙上必须佩戴头盔。

senses.definition: to show or describe someone or something in a particular way

examples.text: The book portrays the scientist as a kind and patient man.

translations.zh: 这本书把那位科学家描绘成一个善良而有耐心的人。

senses.usageNote: Common pattern: 'portray someone as something'.

senses.definition: a long search for something difficult to find

examples.text: The team continued their quest for a cure.

translations.zh: 团队继续寻找治疗方法。

senses.definition: a comparison that explains one thing by showing how it is like another

examples.text: The teacher used an analogy with water pipes to explain electricity.

translations.zh: 老师用水管作类比来解释电流。

senses.usageNote: Say 'draw an analogy between A and B' or 'by analogy with'.

senses.definition: to control or limit something, especially something bad

examples.text: We need to curb the amount of sugar we eat.

translations.zh: 我们需要控制糖的摄入量。

senses.usageNote: In American English 'curb' is also the edge of the pavement; British English spells that 'kerb'.

senses.definition: to officially choose someone or something for a purpose

examples.text: This area is designated for bicycle parking.

translations.zh: 这片区域被指定用于停放自行车。

senses.definition: without hope or comfort; cold and empty

examples.text: The weather was grey and bleak all week.

translations.zh: 整整一周天气都阴沉寒冷。

senses.definition: to take something away from someone or prevent them from having it

examples.text: Too much screen time can deprive children of sleep.

translations.zh: 屏幕时间过长会让孩子缺乏睡眠。

senses.usageNote: Pattern: 'deprive someone of something'.

senses.definition: the official power to make decisions or laws in a certain area

translations.zh: 管辖权；司法权；管辖范围

examples.text: The park is under the jurisdiction of the city council.

translations.zh: 这座公园归市议会管辖。

senses.usageNote: Common patterns: 'under the jurisdiction of', 'have jurisdiction over'.

senses.definition: to choose one thing instead of another

examples.text: Most students opted for the science trip.

translations.zh: 大多数学生选择了科学考察之旅。

senses.usageNote: Patterns: 'opt for something', 'opt to do something', 'opt out of something'.

senses.definition: the best possible

examples.text: Plants need optimal light to grow well.

translations.zh: 植物需要最适宜的光照才能长得好。

senses.definition: to cause a reaction, especially a strong one

examples.text: The article provoked a lively debate in class.

translations.zh: 那篇文章在课堂上引起了热烈的讨论。

senses.definition: to control the direction of a vehicle, or guide a situation

examples.text: She steered the conversation towards a happier topic.

translations.zh: 她把话题引向了一个更愉快的方向。

senses.definition: a formal statement that something is true; or clear proof of something

examples.text: The full stadium was testimony to the team's popularity.

translations.zh: 座无虚席的体育场证明了这支球队的受欢迎程度。

senses.definition: a typical pattern or model of how something works

examples.text: Spaced repetition shifted the paradigm for self-study.

translations.zh: 间隔重复改变了自学的范式。

senses.usageNote: The 'g' is silent in the noun but pronounced in 'paradigmatic'.

senses.definition: although; even though

examples.text: The plan worked, albeit more slowly than we hoped.

translations.zh: 这个计划奏效了，尽管比我们希望的要慢。

senses.usageNote: 'Albeit' is followed by a word or phrase, not a full clause: 'albeit slowly', not 'albeit it was slow'.

senses.definition: to begin

examples.text: The ceremony will commence at ten o'clock.

senses.usageNote: Very formal; in speech 'start' or 'begin' is more natural.

senses.definition: able to be believed or trusted

examples.text: She gave a credible explanation for being late.

translations.zh: 她对迟到给出了一个可信的解释。

senses.usageNote: Don't confuse 'credible' (believable) with 'credulous' (too ready to believe).

senses.definition: the force that slows things when they rub together; disagreement between people

examples.text: Friction between your hands makes them warm.

senses.definition: necessary and important as part of a whole

translations.zh: 不可或缺的；构成整体所必需的

examples.text: Music is an integral part of the festival.

translations.zh: 音乐是这个节日不可或缺的一部分。

senses.usageNote: Common: 'an integral part of something', 'integral to something'.

senses.definition: to show something clearly, or to appear clearly

examples.text: His interest in science manifested itself at an early age.

translations.zh: 他对科学的兴趣在很小的时候就显露出来了。

senses.definition: coming before the main part of an event or activity

examples.text: The preliminary results look very promising.

translations.zh: 初步结果看起来很有希望。

senses.definition: careful and detailed examination

examples.text: The plans came under close scrutiny from experts.

translations.zh: 这些计划受到了专家的严格审查。

senses.usageNote: Common phrases: 'under scrutiny', 'close scrutiny', 'public scrutiny'.

senses.definition: to express ideas or feelings clearly in words

examples.text: She articulated her ideas clearly in the debate.

translations.zh: 她在辩论中清楚地表达了自己的观点。

senses.usageNote: As an adjective, 'articulate' /ɑːˈtɪkjələt/ means able to speak clearly and well: an articulate student.

senses.definition: to make something stronger or more secure; to combine things

examples.text: Doing exercises helps you consolidate what you learned in class.

translations.zh: 做练习有助于巩固课堂上学到的知识。

senses.definition: the freedom to decide what to do; care not to share private information

examples.text: Homework is set at the teacher's discretion.

translations.zh: 作业由老师自行决定布置。

senses.usageNote: 'Use your discretion' means make your own sensible decision.

senses.definition: to use power, influence or effort

examples.text: Friends can exert a strong influence on each other.

translations.zh: 朋友之间会相互产生很大影响。

senses.usageNote: 'Exert yourself' means to make a big physical or mental effort.

senses.definition: a small piece that has broken off something

examples.text: We found fragments of an old pot in the garden.

translations.zh: 我们在花园里发现了一些旧陶罐碎片。

senses.definition: not well known, or difficult to understand

examples.text: The song was written by an obscure band from the 1970s.

translations.zh: 这首歌是一个七十年代鲜为人知的乐队写的。

senses.definition: to hide something or make it hard to see

examples.text: Clouds obscured the top of the mountain.

senses.definition: expected or likely to become something in the future

examples.text: The school holds an open day for prospective students.

translations.zh: 学校为未来的学生举办开放日。

senses.definition: stiff and hard to bend, or not easy to change

examples.text: The school has rigid rules about uniforms.

translations.zh: 这所学校对校服有严格的规定。

senses.definition: an amount that is more than what is needed

examples.text: The farm gives its surplus of vegetables to a food bank.

translations.zh: 农场把多余的蔬菜捐给食物银行。

senses.definition: seeming reasonable or likely to be true

examples.text: It's a plausible explanation, but the data says otherwise.

translations.zh: 这是个看似合理的解释，但数据并非如此。

senses.usageNote: Often carries a hint of doubt: plausible is not the same as proven.

senses.definition: to make something wider or include more

examples.text: Travel can broaden your understanding of other cultures.

translations.zh: 旅行可以加深你对其他文化的了解。

senses.usageNote: Very common in 'broaden your horizons' (experience new things).

senses.definition: to see or show the difference between things

examples.text: Young children often can't differentiate between fact and fiction.

translations.zh: 小孩子常常分不清事实和虚构。

senses.usageNote: Use 'differentiate between A and B' or 'differentiate A from B'.

senses.definition: to publicly say that you support someone or something

examples.text: The doctors endorsed the new healthy eating plan.

translations.zh: 医生们支持这项新的健康饮食计划。

senses.definition: power or influence that helps you get what you want

examples.text: Good exam results give you more leverage when choosing a university.

translations.zh: 好的考试成绩让你在选择大学时更有优势。

senses.definition: to use something you have to gain an advantage

examples.text: The company leveraged its brand to sell new products.

translations.zh: 这家公司借助自身品牌推销新产品。

senses.definition: someone who works in a skilled job, such as medicine or law

examples.text: You should see a medical practitioner about that cough.

translations.zh: 你应该找医生看看你的咳嗽。

senses.usageNote: In British English, a 'general practitioner' (GP) is a family doctor.

senses.definition: a person who receives something

examples.text: She was the recipient of this year's art prize.

translations.zh: 她是今年艺术奖的获得者。

senses.definition: something that causes growth, activity or a reaction

examples.text: The new park acted as a stimulus for local business.

translations.zh: 新公园对当地商业起到了促进作用。

senses.definition: an official decision in a court, or an opinion after testing something

examples.text: The judges' verdict was that our cake was the best.

translations.zh: 评委的结论是我们的蛋糕最好。

senses.definition: responsible for your actions and expected to explain them

translations.zh: 负有责任的；应作解释的

examples.text: Team leaders are accountable for the results of their team.

translations.zh: 团队负责人要对团队的成果负责。

senses.usageNote: Use 'accountable to someone for something': We are accountable to our customers for the quality.

senses.definition: to become worse

examples.text: The old books had deteriorated because of the damp.

translations.zh: 这些旧书因受潮而损坏了。

senses.usageNote: Pronounce all five syllables: de-TEER-ee-uh-rate.

senses.definition: extremely important and urgent

translations.zh: 必要的；紧迫的；极重要的

examples.text: It is imperative that you wear a helmet when cycling.

senses.usageNote: Pattern: 'It is imperative that someone (should) do something' or 'It is imperative to do something'.

senses.definition: in a straight line, or developing in clear stages one after another

examples.text: The story is not linear; it jumps backwards and forwards.

translations.zh: 这个故事不是线性的，它前后跳跃。

senses.definition: strange or unusual; also belonging only to one person, place or thing

examples.text: There was a peculiar smell coming from the fridge.

translations.zh: 冰箱里传出一股奇怪的气味。

senses.usageNote: 'Peculiar to' means found only in: 'a plant peculiar to this island'.

senses.definition: to improve something by making small changes

examples.text: We refined our design after testing it with users.

translations.zh: 在用户测试之后，我们改进了设计。

senses.definition: expressing opinions loudly and often; also connected with the voice

examples.text: Parents were very vocal in their support for the new park.

translations.zh: 家长们大力支持建新公园。

senses.definition: to make two different ideas or facts fit together

examples.text: It is hard to reconcile the two accounts.

translations.zh: 很难把这两种说法调和起来。

senses.definition: the state of being in a straight line or agreeing with something

examples.text: Check the alignment of the pictures before you hang them.

translations.zh: 挂画之前先检查一下是否对齐。

senses.definition: to create a strong relationship; to make an illegal copy

examples.text: The two schools forged a strong friendship through sport.

translations.zh: 两所学校通过体育运动建立了深厚的友谊。

senses.usageNote: 'Forge ahead' means to make fast progress.

senses.definition: going to happen soon; willing to give information

translations.zh: 即将到来的；乐于提供信息的

examples.text: Tickets for the forthcoming concert are on sale now.

translations.zh: 即将举行的音乐会门票正在出售。

senses.definition: existing in large amounts; more than enough

examples.text: The forest has an abundant supply of fruit in summer.

translations.zh: 这片森林夏天有丰富的果实。

senses.usageNote: Say 'abundant in something': The river is abundant in fish.

senses.definition: to follow rules or behave like most other people

examples.text: Some students feel pressure to conform to their friends' tastes.

translations.zh: 一些学生感到有压力要迎合朋友的喜好。

senses.usageNote: Use 'conform to/with something'.

senses.definition: to change the direction or use of something

translations.zh: 使转向；转移（注意力）；挪用

examples.text: Traffic was diverted because of roadworks.

translations.zh: 因为道路施工，车辆被引导绕行。

senses.definition: to judge or measure something

examples.text: It's hard to gauge how long the journey will take.

translations.zh: 很难估计这趟旅程需要多长时间。

senses.usageNote: Spelling: 'au' but pronounced like 'gage'.

senses.definition: temporary, lasting until something permanent is ready

examples.text: An interim coach will lead the team until June.

translations.zh: 一位临时教练将带领球队到六月。

senses.usageNote: 'In the interim' means in the time between two events.

senses.definition: the ability to read and write; also, skill in a particular area

translations.zh: 读写能力；（某方面的）素养

examples.text: The charity works to improve literacy among young children.

translations.zh: 这个慈善机构致力于提高幼儿的读写能力。

senses.usageNote: Also used for other skills: 'digital literacy', 'financial literacy'.

senses.definition: to balance one effect with an opposite effect

examples.text: The higher price is offset by the better quality.

translations.zh: 较高的价格被更好的质量抵消了。

senses.definition: a person who had a job before someone else, or a thing that came before another

examples.text: The new phone is lighter than its predecessor.

translations.zh: 新款手机比上一代更轻。

senses.definition: a question, especially one asking for official information

examples.text: If you have any queries, please contact the office.

translations.zh: 如有任何疑问，请联系办公室。

senses.definition: not moving or changing

examples.text: Prices have remained static for two years.

translations.zh: 价格两年来一直没有变化。

senses.definition: money given by a government or organisation to reduce costs

examples.text: Farmers receive a subsidy for planting trees.

translations.zh: 农民种树可以获得补贴。

senses.definition: by which; through which (formal)

examples.text: The school has a system whereby older pupils help younger ones.

translations.zh: 学校有一套高年级学生帮助低年级学生的制度。

senses.definition: dealing with problems in a practical way rather than by theory

examples.text: A pragmatic goal beats an ambitious one you abandon.

translations.zh: 务实的目标胜过被你放弃的宏大目标。

senses.definition: a standard used to measure or judge other things

examples.text: This test is a benchmark for measuring reading progress.

translations.zh: 这项测试是衡量阅读进步的基准。

senses.definition: to fix something firmly inside something else

examples.text: A small stone was embedded in the tyre.

translations.zh: 一颗小石子嵌进了轮胎里。

senses.usageNote: Often passive: 'be embedded in something'. Also used for videos placed inside web pages.

senses.definition: shared by a whole group; not specific; without a brand name

translations.zh: 通用的；一般的；无商标的

examples.text: Avoid generic phrases like 'it was nice' in your essay.

translations.zh: 写作文时避免使用“很好”之类的泛泛之词。

senses.definition: how often something happens, especially something bad

examples.text: The incidence of colds rises in winter.

translations.zh: 冬天感冒的发病率上升。

senses.usageNote: Don't confuse 'incidence' (rate) with 'incident' (a single event) or 'incidents' (plural of incident).

senses.definition: to get something back, or find stored information

examples.text: I retrieved my ball from the neighbour's garden.

translations.zh: 我从邻居家的花园里拿回了我的球。

senses.definition: to grow or develop very well and be successful

examples.text: These plants thrive in warm, sunny places.

translations.zh: 这些植物在温暖、阳光充足的地方长得很好。

senses.usageNote: Common pattern: 'thrive on something', e.g. 'She thrives on challenges.'

senses.definition: real and definite enough to be seen or measured

examples.text: After a month there were tangible results.

translations.zh: 一个月后有了实在的成果。

senses.definition: saying what you think directly, without trying to be polite; not sharp

examples.text: To be blunt, your essay needs a lot more work.

translations.zh: 说实话，你的文章还需要下很大功夫。

senses.definition: a lack of something that is needed

examples.text: A vitamin deficiency can make you feel tired.

translations.zh: 缺乏维生素会让人感到疲倦。

senses.definition: extreme and having a strong or sudden effect

examples.text: The company made drastic changes to its website.

translations.zh: 公司对网站进行了大刀阔斧的改动。

senses.definition: to become bigger, more serious or more intense

examples.text: The small argument quickly escalated into a big quarrel.

translations.zh: 小争执很快升级为大吵。

senses.definition: an experienced person who advises and helps someone less experienced

examples.text: Each new employee is given a mentor for the first year.

translations.zh: 每位新员工第一年都会配一位导师。

senses.definition: belonging to or run by a town or city government

examples.text: We swim at the municipal pool every Saturday.

translations.zh: 我们每周六在市立游泳池游泳。

senses.definition: to think that something is true although you are not certain

examples.text: I presume you have already had lunch.

translations.zh: 我猜你已经吃过午饭了。

senses.definition: very careful and thorough, following strict rules

examples.text: All new toys go through rigorous safety tests.

translations.zh: 所有新玩具都要经过严格的安全测试。

senses.definition: a law that has been formally written down

examples.text: The statute protects the rights of young workers.

translations.zh: 该法规保护年轻工人的权利。

senses.usageNote: Do not confuse with 'statue', a figure made of stone or metal.

senses.definition: the quality of being open and honest so people can see what is happening

examples.text: Parents asked for more transparency about how money is spent.

translations.zh: 家长要求提高资金使用的透明度。

senses.definition: a difference between two things that should be the same

examples.text: There's a discrepancy between the two figures.

translations.zh: 两个数字之间存在差异。

senses.definition: more than enough

examples.text: There is ample time to finish the task before lunch.

translations.zh: 午饭前有充足的时间完成任务。

senses.usageNote: Usually before uncountable or plural nouns: ample space, ample evidence, ample opportunities.

senses.definition: following one after another without a break

examples.text: It rained for five consecutive days.

senses.definition: to make someone decide not to do something

examples.text: The heavy rain did not deter the runners.

senses.usageNote: Pattern: 'deter someone from doing something'.

senses.definition: a serious attempt to do something

examples.text: Building the robot was a team endeavour.

translations.zh: 制作这个机器人是团队共同努力的结果。

senses.usageNote: British spelling 'endeavour'; American 'endeavor'. It is also a formal verb: 'We endeavour to reply within a day.'

senses.definition: to develop a plan or idea carefully; to express something carefully

examples.text: The group formulated a plan to clean up the park.

translations.zh: 小组制定了一个清理公园的计划。

senses.definition: not available in large amounts; not enough

examples.text: Water is scarce in the desert.

senses.usageNote: Do not confuse 'scarce' with 'scared'. The noun is 'scarcity'.

senses.definition: next to or very near something

examples.text: Our classroom is adjacent to the library.

translations.zh: 我们的教室紧挨着图书馆。

senses.definition: to discuss something with others before deciding; to give an official honour

examples.text: The judges conferred for a few minutes before announcing the winner.

translations.zh: 评委们商议了几分钟后宣布了获胜者。

senses.definition: broken pieces left after something has been destroyed

examples.text: The beach was covered with debris after the storm.

translations.zh: 暴风雨过后，海滩上满是残骸碎片。

senses.usageNote: Uncountable: 'a lot of debris', never 'debrises'. The final 's' is silent.

senses.definition: to be a perfect example of an idea or quality

examples.text: The young volunteer embodies the spirit of kindness.

translations.zh: 这位年轻的志愿者体现了善良的精神。

senses.definition: dangerous, especially to health or safety

examples.text: Hazardous chemicals must be stored carefully.

translations.zh: 危险化学品必须妥善储存。

senses.definition: to form an opinion from the information you have

examples.text: From her smile, I inferred that she had passed.

translations.zh: 从她的笑容中，我推断她通过了。

senses.usageNote: The speaker 'implies'; the listener 'infers'. Don't mix them up.

senses.definition: to prevent or slow down something; to make someone feel unable to act freely

examples.text: Cold weather inhibits the growth of plants.

translations.zh: 寒冷天气抑制植物生长。

senses.definition: to stay somewhere longer than usual or than necessary

examples.text: The smell of fresh bread lingered in the kitchen.

translations.zh: 新鲜面包的香味在厨房里久久不散。

senses.definition: complete control of a business or activity by one company or person

examples.text: One company has a monopoly on the island's ferry service.

translations.zh: 一家公司垄断了岛上的渡轮服务。

senses.usageNote: Say 'a monopoly on/of something'.

senses.definition: an idea that a theory or argument is based on

examples.text: The story's premise is that animals can talk.

translations.zh: 这个故事的前提是动物会说话。

senses.usageNote: 'Premises' (plural) also means a building and its land: 'No parking on the premises.'

senses.definition: calm control of your feelings or behaviour

examples.text: He showed great restraint when the other team cheated.

translations.zh: 对方作弊时，他表现得非常克制。

senses.definition: to bring something back to life, health or popularity

examples.text: The village revived an old tradition of spring dancing.

translations.zh: 村子恢复了春季跳舞的古老传统。

senses.definition: to guess possible answers without having all the facts

examples.text: Scientists speculate that there may be water on the moon.

translations.zh: 科学家推测月球上可能有水。

senses.usageNote: Use 'speculate about/on something' or 'speculate that...'.

senses.definition: the state of being logical, true or officially acceptable

examples.text: Some experts question the validity of the survey.

translations.zh: 一些专家质疑这项调查的有效性。

senses.definition: common in a particular place or at a particular time

examples.text: That mistake is prevalent among learners of English.

translations.zh: 这个错误在英语学习者中很普遍。

senses.definition: a strong negative reaction from many people

examples.text: The price rise caused a backlash from customers.

translations.zh: 涨价引起了顾客的强烈反对。

senses.definition: making you feel nervous or less confident because it seems difficult

translations.zh: 令人生畏的；使人畏缩的

examples.text: Learning a new language can seem daunting at first.

translations.zh: 学一门新语言起初可能让人望而生畏。

senses.usageNote: Common: 'a daunting task', 'a daunting challenge'.

senses.definition: to change the shape or meaning of something so it is no longer true or accurate

examples.text: The curved mirror distorted our faces.

translations.zh: 那面曲面镜把我们的脸照得变了形。

senses.definition: to involve something as a necessary part

examples.text: Keeping a pet entails a lot of responsibility.

translations.zh: 养宠物意味着要承担很多责任。

senses.usageNote: Not used in continuous forms: say 'What does the job entail?', not 'is entailing'.

senses.definition: very impressive, powerful or difficult to deal with

translations.zh: 令人敬畏的；难对付的；强大的

examples.text: The champion is a formidable opponent.

translations.zh: 这位冠军是个难以对付的对手。

senses.definition: to control and use the power of something

examples.text: Solar panels harness energy from the sun.

translations.zh: 太阳能电池板利用太阳的能量。

senses.definition: a problem you must deal with before you can make progress

examples.text: The last hurdle is getting permission from our parents.

translations.zh: 最后一关是得到父母的同意。

senses.definition: to cause something to happen; to persuade someone

examples.text: Warm milk can help induce sleep.

senses.definition: to move from one place to another, especially with the seasons

examples.text: These birds migrate south every autumn.

translations.zh: 这些鸟每年秋天向南迁徙。

senses.definition: having many small parts arranged in a complicated way

examples.text: The Thai script has an intricate system of tone marks.

translations.zh: 泰文有一套复杂精细的声调符号系统。

senses.definition: a total made by adding several amounts together

examples.text: Our team won with an aggregate of 95 points over two rounds.

translations.zh: 我们队两轮总分95分获胜。

senses.definition: something that causes an important change or event

examples.text: The school trip was a catalyst for his love of science.

translations.zh: 那次学校旅行激发了他对科学的热爱。

senses.usageNote: Use 'a catalyst for (change)'.

senses.definition: to start something new and important; to get on a ship or plane

examples.text: She embarked on a journey around the world.

translations.zh: 她开始了一次环球旅行。

senses.usageNote: Use 'embark on/upon something': embark on a career, a project, an adventure.

senses.definition: to know that something will happen before it does

examples.text: Nobody could foresee how popular the game would become.

translations.zh: 谁也没预料到这个游戏会这么受欢迎。

senses.usageNote: The adjective 'unforeseen' (not expected) is common: unforeseen problems.

senses.definition: to make it difficult for something to happen

examples.text: Noise can hinder your ability to concentrate.

translations.zh: 噪音会妨碍你集中注意力。

senses.definition: to watch and organise a job or activity to check it is done well

examples.text: A teacher will oversee the science experiment.

translations.zh: 一位老师将监督这个科学实验。

senses.usageNote: Do not confuse with 'overlook', which means to fail to notice something.

senses.definition: not important or serious

examples.text: They argued about something trivial, like who sits where.

translations.zh: 他们为谁坐哪里这样的小事争吵。

senses.definition: equipment used for a particular scientific or technical job

examples.text: The students set up the apparatus for the chemistry test.

translations.zh: 学生们为化学实验安装了仪器。

senses.usageNote: Usually uncountable: 'a piece of apparatus'.

senses.definition: to take the place of something; to force people or animals to leave their home

examples.text: Robots may displace some workers in factories.

translations.zh: 机器人可能会取代工厂里的一些工人。

senses.definition: to imagine or expect something in the future

examples.text: I envisage a garden full of flowers here.

translations.zh: 我设想这里将是一个开满鲜花的花园。

senses.usageNote: British English; American English prefers 'envision'. Follow with '-ing': 'I envisage working abroad'.

senses.definition: about to happen very soon

examples.text: Dark clouds showed that a storm was imminent.

translations.zh: 乌云密布，暴风雨即将来临。

senses.usageNote: Don't confuse 'imminent' (very soon) with 'eminent' (famous and respected).

senses.definition: to appear large and unclear, or to seem about to happen in a worrying way

examples.text: With exams looming, the library was full every evening.

translations.zh: 考试临近，图书馆每天晚上都坐满了人。

senses.definition: a person who gives money or support to an artist or organisation; also a customer

examples.text: She is a patron of the local children's theatre.

translations.zh: 她是当地儿童剧院的赞助人。

senses.definition: likely to suffer from something or do something, usually bad

examples.text: This area is prone to flooding in winter.

translations.zh: 这个地区冬天容易发生洪水。

senses.usageNote: Use 'prone to something' or 'prone to do something'; also as a suffix: 'accident-prone'.

senses.definition: happening naturally and without planning

examples.text: The audience burst into spontaneous applause.

translations.zh: 观众自发地爆发出掌声。

senses.definition: a person or group with an interest in how something succeeds

examples.text: Parents, pupils and teachers are all stakeholders in the school.

translations.zh: 家长、学生和老师都是学校的利益相关者。

senses.definition: the background to a scene or event

examples.text: The mountains made a stunning backdrop for our photos.

translations.zh: 群山为我们的照片提供了绝美的背景。

senses.usageNote: 'Against a backdrop of' is often used for situations: against a backdrop of rising prices.

senses.definition: to limit what someone or something can do

examples.text: Our plans were constrained by a small budget.

translations.zh: 我们的计划受到预算不足的限制。

senses.usageNote: The noun 'constraint' is very common: time constraints, budget constraints.

senses.definition: the ability to understand and share another person's feelings

examples.text: Good doctors show empathy towards their patients.

translations.zh: 好医生会对病人抱有同理心。

senses.usageNote: 'Empathy' means feeling with someone; 'sympathy' means feeling sorry for them.

senses.definition: one part or side of a situation, subject or character

examples.text: Music is an important facet of school life.

translations.zh: 音乐是校园生活的一个重要方面。

senses.definition: an impressive action that needs skill, strength or courage

examples.text: Climbing the mountain in one day was quite a feat.

translations.zh: 一天之内登上那座山真是了不起。

senses.usageNote: Often 'no mean feat' = a difficult achievement. Don't confuse with 'feet'.

senses.definition: the level of confidence and good spirits in a person or group

examples.text: Winning the first match boosted the team's morale.

translations.zh: 赢得第一场比赛提升了球队的士气。

senses.usageNote: Do not confuse 'morale' /məˈrɑːl/ with 'moral' /ˈmɒrəl/, which is about right and wrong.

senses.definition: a mistake caused by not noticing something; also the job of watching over an activity

examples.text: Leaving her name off the list was an oversight.

translations.zh: 名单上漏掉她的名字是个疏忽。

senses.usageNote: Careful: 'oversight' can mean both a mistake and supervision.

senses.definition: the respect and admiration that someone or something gets because of success or quality

examples.text: Winning the award brought the school great prestige.

translations.zh: 获得这个奖项给学校带来了极高的声望。

senses.definition: the combination of different ideas or things into a whole

examples.text: Her essay is a synthesis of several different theories.

translations.zh: 她的论文综合了几种不同的理论。

senses.definition: to make something bad, such as pain or a problem, less severe

examples.text: A cool cloth can alleviate the pain of a headache.

senses.usageNote: Use for problems or suffering: alleviate pain, poverty, stress. Don't use it for things that are simply large.

senses.definition: believing that people usually act only for their own benefit

translations.zh: 愤世嫉俗的；认为人皆自私的

examples.text: He has a cynical view of advertising.

senses.definition: lasting a long time without breaking

examples.text: These boots are made of durable leather.

translations.zh: 这双靴子是用耐用的皮革做的。

senses.definition: difficult to find, catch or achieve

examples.text: The snow leopard is an elusive animal.

translations.zh: 雪豹是一种难觅踪迹的动物。

senses.definition: something that is a mix of two different things

translations.zh: 混合物；杂交品种；混合动力车

examples.text: A mule is a hybrid of a horse and a donkey.

translations.zh: 骡子是马和驴的杂交后代。

senses.definition: being part of the basic nature of something

examples.text: Curiosity is an intrinsic part of childhood.

translations.zh: 好奇心是童年固有的一部分。

senses.usageNote: 'Intrinsic motivation' means doing something because you enjoy it, not for a reward.

senses.definition: an important event or stage in the development of something

examples.text: Learning to walk is a big milestone for a baby.

translations.zh: 学会走路是婴儿成长的一个重要里程碑。

senses.definition: a short, interesting story about a real event

examples.text: Grandpa told a funny anecdote about his first day at work.

translations.zh: 爷爷讲了一件他第一天上班的趣事。

senses.definition: probably not honest or true; feeling doubt

examples.text: The advert made some dubious claims about the cream.

translations.zh: 这则广告对这款面霜的宣传有些可疑。

senses.usageNote: 'Be dubious about something' means to feel unsure about it.

senses.definition: to give someone the confidence, power or right to do something

examples.text: The course empowers young people to start their own projects.

translations.zh: 这门课程让年轻人有能力开展自己的项目。

senses.definition: to bring a feeling or memory into your mind

examples.text: The smell of cookies evoked memories of Grandma's kitchen.

translations.zh: 饼干的香味让我想起了奶奶的厨房。

senses.definition: allowed not to do or pay something others must

examples.text: Students with a note from home are exempt from sports today.

translations.zh: 持家长证明的学生今天可以免上体育课。

senses.usageNote: Use 'exempt from something'.

senses.definition: a change in the genes of a living thing

examples.text: A rare mutation gave the tiger its white fur.

translations.zh: 一种罕见的基因突变使这只老虎长出了白色的毛。

senses.definition: well known for something bad

translations.zh: 臭名昭著的；声名狼藉的

examples.text: This road is notorious for traffic jams.

senses.usageNote: 'Notorious' is negative; for good fame use 'famous' or 'renowned'.

senses.definition: to exist widely, or to win after a struggle

examples.text: In the end, common sense prevailed.

senses.definition: language used to persuade people, sometimes without real meaning

examples.text: The students studied the rhetoric of famous speeches.

translations.zh: 学生们研究了著名演讲的修辞手法。

senses.definition: to go around or avoid something

examples.text: We bypassed the busy town centre by taking the ring road.

translations.zh: 我们走环城路绕开了繁忙的市中心。

senses.definition: final and not able to be changed; the best of its kind

examples.text: This is the definitive guide to birds of Britain.

translations.zh: 这是关于英国鸟类最权威的指南。

senses.usageNote: Don't confuse with 'definite' (certain, clear): a definite answer vs. the definitive book on a subject.

senses.definition: the joining together of different things into one

examples.text: The restaurant serves a fusion of Thai and Italian food.

translations.zh: 这家餐厅供应泰意融合菜。

senses.definition: extremely useful

examples.text: Your advice has been invaluable to me.

translations.zh: 你的建议对我非常宝贵。

senses.usageNote: 'Invaluable' means very valuable, not 'not valuable'. The word for no value is 'worthless'.

senses.definition: a job or activity that suits someone well, or a small specialised area of a market

translations.zh: 适合的位置；细分市场；利基

examples.text: The shop found a niche selling handmade toys.

translations.zh: 这家店找到了销售手工玩具的细分市场。

senses.usageNote: British pronunciation is usually /niːʃ/; /nɪtʃ/ is also heard.

senses.definition: to make something bad less severe

examples.text: Interval fuzzing mitigates spikes in daily workload.

translations.zh: 间隔抖动可以缓解每日学习量的高峰。

senses.usageNote: 'Mitigate' reduces harm; 'militate' means to be a strong influence against. 'Mitigate against' is an error.

senses.definition: to support or make something stronger

examples.text: Winning the first match bolstered the team's confidence.

translations.zh: 首场比赛获胜增强了队员们的信心。

senses.definition: short and clear, with no unnecessary words

examples.text: Write a concise summary of the article in fifty words.

translations.zh: 用五十个词简明概括这篇文章。

senses.definition: to include many different things

examples.text: The course encompasses art, music and drama.

translations.zh: 这门课程涵盖了美术、音乐和戏剧。

senses.definition: most important or best known

examples.text: She is one of the foremost experts on bees.

translations.zh: 她是研究蜜蜂最顶尖的专家之一。

senses.usageNote: 'First and foremost' means 'most importantly'.

senses.definition: to damage something so it works less well

examples.text: Loud music can impair your hearing over time.

translations.zh: 长期听大声的音乐会损害听力。

senses.definition: relating to the side of something, or moving sideways

examples.text: Solving the puzzle needs some lateral thinking.

translations.zh: 解开这个谜题需要一些横向思维。

senses.usageNote: 'Lateral thinking' means solving problems in creative, unexpected ways.

senses.definition: existing in name only; or very small compared with the real value

examples.text: The museum charges a nominal fee for students.

translations.zh: 博物馆对学生只收象征性的费用。

senses.definition: the beginning of something, especially something unpleasant

examples.text: We planted the bulbs before the onset of winter.

translations.zh: 我们在入冬之前种下了球茎。

senses.definition: a situation or statement that seems impossible because it has two opposite facts

examples.text: It's a paradox that the more you rest, the more tired you feel.

translations.zh: 休息得越多反而觉得越累，这真是个悖论。

senses.definition: the reasons behind a decision or plan

examples.text: Can you explain the rationale behind the new rule?

translations.zh: 你能解释一下这条新规定背后的理由吗？

senses.definition: famous and admired for a special skill or quality

examples.text: The city is renowned for its beautiful gardens.

translations.zh: 这座城市以美丽的花园而闻名。

senses.usageNote: Say 'renowned for something' or 'renowned as something'.

senses.definition: to encourage someone or something to do more or develop faster

examples.text: Her success spurred her friends to try harder.

translations.zh: 她的成功激励朋友们更加努力。

senses.usageNote: 'On the spur of the moment' means suddenly, without planning.

senses.definition: very active, strong and full of energy

translations.zh: 剧烈的；充满活力的；强有力的

examples.text: Thirty minutes of vigorous exercise a day keeps you fit.

translations.zh: 每天三十分钟的剧烈运动能让你保持健康。

senses.definition: connected with selling goods in large amounts to shops; also affecting almost everything

examples.text: The shop buys its fruit at wholesale prices.

translations.zh: 这家店以批发价购进水果。

senses.definition: quick and full of energy

examples.text: We went for a brisk walk after dinner.

translations.zh: 晚饭后我们快步走了一圈。

senses.definition: too large or too small compared with something else

translations.zh: 不成比例的；过大或过小的

examples.text: He spent a disproportionate amount of time on the first question.

translations.zh: 他在第一道题上花了过多时间。

senses.definition: to slowly damage or wear away something

examples.text: The sea has eroded the cliffs over many years.

translations.zh: 多年来大海侵蚀了悬崖。

senses.definition: to light something up; to help explain something

examples.text: Lanterns illuminated the garden at night.

senses.definition: something that is different from what is normal or expected

examples.text: One strange result was an anomaly in the experiment.

translations.zh: 一个奇怪的结果是实验中的异常数据。

senses.definition: a person's natural character

examples.text: She has a cheerful disposition and rarely complains.

senses.definition: to increase a feeling or effect

examples.text: The music heightened the tension in the film.

translations.zh: 音乐增加了电影的紧张气氛。

senses.definition: using the basic, exact meaning of a word, not an imaginative meaning

examples.text: A literal translation of the joke doesn't make sense in Chinese.

translations.zh: 把这个笑话按字面翻译成中文就说不通了。

senses.usageNote: 'Literally' is often used informally just for emphasis, but in careful writing it means 'exactly as stated'.

senses.definition: producing a lot of money

examples.text: Designing apps can be a lucrative career.

translations.zh: 设计应用程序可以是一份收入丰厚的职业。

senses.definition: trusting others too easily because of a lack of experience

examples.text: It was naive of me to believe the advert.

translations.zh: 我竟然相信了那则广告，真是太天真了。

senses.usageNote: Sometimes spelt 'naïve'. It is usually negative, unlike Chinese '天真' which can be positive.

senses.definition: the start of something

examples.text: Make the rules clear from the outset.

translations.zh: 从一开始就把规则讲清楚。

senses.usageNote: Almost always used in 'at the outset' or 'from the outset'.

senses.definition: a judgement of how good or valuable someone or something is

examples.text: Every employee has a yearly appraisal with their manager.

translations.zh: 每位员工每年都要与经理进行一次绩效评估。

senses.definition: the end of something that used to exist

examples.text: The demise of the old cinema made many people sad.

translations.zh: 老电影院的关闭让许多人很难过。

senses.definition: to improve the quality of something by adding to it

examples.text: Learning music enriches children's lives.

translations.zh: 学习音乐能丰富孩子们的生活。

senses.definition: to change often, going up and down

examples.text: Temperatures fluctuate a lot in spring.

senses.definition: to care for and help someone or something grow and develop

examples.text: Good teachers nurture their students' curiosity.

translations.zh: 好老师会培养学生的好奇心。

senses.definition: to happen or come before something else

examples.text: A short film preceded the main concert.

translations.zh: 主场音乐会之前先播放了一部短片。

senses.usageNote: Do not confuse with 'proceed', which means to continue.

senses.definition: to try very hard to achieve something

examples.text: We always strive to give our customers the best service.

translations.zh: 我们始终努力为顾客提供最好的服务。

senses.usageNote: Use 'strive to do something' or 'strive for something'.

senses.definition: likely to change suddenly and unexpectedly

translations.zh: 易变的；不稳定的；易挥发的

examples.text: Fuel prices have been very volatile this year.

translations.zh: 今年燃料价格波动很大。

senses.definition: to make a sound louder or an effect stronger

examples.text: Microphones amplify the speaker's voice in a large hall.

translations.zh: 在大礼堂里，麦克风能放大演讲者的声音。

senses.definition: to make a proposal into law; to act out a story

examples.text: The children enacted a scene from their favourite book.

translations.zh: 孩子们表演了他们最喜欢的书中的一个场景。

senses.definition: something that makes a process happen or move faster

examples.text: The award gave new impetus to her writing career.

translations.zh: 这个奖项为她的写作生涯注入了新动力。

senses.usageNote: Uncountable: say 'give impetus to' or 'provide the impetus for'.

senses.definition: honest and direct, even about difficult things

examples.text: She gave a candid answer about her mistakes.

translations.zh: 她坦率地谈了自己的错误。

senses.definition: to spread out and go in different directions

examples.text: The crowd dispersed after the fireworks ended.

translations.zh: 烟花结束后，人群散去了。

senses.definition: to avoid something or someone, often dishonestly

examples.text: He tried to evade the question by changing the subject.

translations.zh: 他试图转移话题来回避这个问题。

senses.definition: a feeling or complaint about being treated unfairly

examples.text: Students can raise any grievance with the school council.

translations.zh: 学生可以向学生会提出任何不满。

senses.definition: easy to understand or use without being taught; based on feelings

translations.zh: 直观的；易懂的；凭直觉的

examples.text: The app has an intuitive design that anyone can use.

translations.zh: 这个应用设计直观，谁都会用。

senses.definition: young and not yet an adult; also, silly in a childish way

translations.zh: 青少年的；幼年的；幼稚的

examples.text: Juvenile birds have brown feathers rather than white ones.

translations.zh: 幼鸟的羽毛是棕色的，而不是白色的。

senses.definition: the detailed planning and organisation of a complicated activity

examples.text: The logistics of taking 200 pupils to the zoo are challenging.

translations.zh: 带200名学生去动物园的组织工作很有挑战性。

senses.usageNote: Takes a plural or singular verb: 'The logistics are/is complicated.'

senses.definition: to organise people or resources so they can work together for a purpose

examples.text: The school mobilised parents to help clean the park.

translations.zh: 学校动员家长帮忙清理公园。

senses.definition: accepted by most people as normal or correct

examples.text: She prefers orthodox teaching methods to new trends.

translations.zh: 比起新潮流，她更喜欢传统的教学方法。

senses.definition: to be more important than something, or to cancel a decision using your authority

examples.text: Safety should override all other concerns.

translations.zh: 安全应当高于其他一切考虑。

senses.definition: extremely important because other things depend on it

examples.text: She played a pivotal role in the team's success.

translations.zh: 她在球队的成功中发挥了关键作用。

senses.definition: a fixed amount or number that is allowed or expected

examples.text: Each fishing boat has a daily quota.

translations.zh: 每条渔船都有每日的捕捞配额。

senses.definition: not needed any more, or more than is necessary

translations.zh: 多余的；冗余的；被裁员的

examples.text: Delete any redundant words from your essay.

translations.zh: 删去作文中所有多余的词。
